mn20:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn20:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn20:2.1: “Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is pursuing the higher mind, from time to time he should give attention to five signs.
mn20:3.1: i “Here, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is giving attention to some sign, and owing to that sign there arise in him evil unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, with hate, and with delusion, then he should give attention to some other sign connected with what is wholesome.
mn20:3.2: When he gives attention to some other sign connected with what is wholesome, then any evil unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, with hate, and with delusion are abandoned in him and subside.
mn20:3.3: With the abandoning of them his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
mn20:3.4: Just as a skilled carpenter or his apprentice might knock out, remove, and extract a coarse peg by means of a fine one,
mn20:3.5: so too…when a bhikkhu gives attention to some other sign connected with what is wholesome…
mn20:3.7: his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
mn20:4.1: ii “If, while he is giving attention to some other sign connected with what is wholesome, there still arise in him evil unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, with hate, and with delusion, then he should examine the danger in those thoughts thus:
mn20:4.2: ‘These thoughts are unwholesome, they are reprehensible, they result in suffering.’
mn20:4.3: When he examines the danger in those thoughts, then any evil unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, with hate, and with delusion are abandoned in him and subside.
mn20:4.4: With the abandoning of them his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
mn20:4.5: Just as a man or a woman, young, youthful, and fond of ornaments, would be horrified, humiliated, and disgusted if the carcass of a snake or a dog or a human being were hung around his or her neck,
mn20:4.6: so too…when a bhikkhu examines the danger in those thoughts…
mn20:4.9: his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
mn20:5.1: iii “If, while he is examining the danger in those thoughts, there still arise in him evil unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, with hate, and with delusion, then he should try to forget those thoughts and should not give attention to them.
mn20:5.2: When he tries to forget those thoughts and does not give attention to them, then any evil unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, with hate, and with delusion are abandoned in him and subside.
mn20:5.3: With the abandoning of them his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
mn20:5.4: Just as a man with good eyes who did not want to see forms that had come within range of sight
mn20:5.5: would either shut his eyes or look away,
mn20:5.6: so too…when a bhikkhu tries to forget those thoughts and does not give attention to them …
mn20:5.7: his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
mn20:6.1: iv “If, while he is trying to forget those thoughts and is not giving attention to them, there still arise in him evil unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, with hate, and with delusion, then he should give attention to stilling the thought-formation of those thoughts.
mn20:6.2: When he gives attention to stilling the thought-formation of those thoughts, then any evil unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, with hate, and with delusion are abandoned in him and subside.
mn20:6.3: With the abandoning of them his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
mn20:6.4: Just as a man walking fast
mn20:6.21: By doing so he would substitute for each grosser posture one that was subtler.
mn20:6.22: So too…when a bhikkhu gives attention to stilling the thought-formation of those thoughts…his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
mn20:7.1: v “If, while he is giving attention to stilling the thought-formation of those thoughts, there still arise in him evil unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, with hate, and with delusion,
mn20:7.2: then, with his teeth clenched and his tongue pressed against the roof of his mouth, he should beat down, constrain, and crush mind with mind.
mn20:7.3: When, with his teeth clenched and his tongue pressed against the roof of his mouth, he beats down, constrains, and crushes mind with mind, then any evil unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, with hate, and with delusion are abandoned in him and subside.
mn20:7.4: With the abandoning of them his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
mn20:7.5: Just as a strong man might seize a weaker man by the head or shoulders and beat him down, constrain him, and crush him,
mn20:7.7: with his teeth clenched and his tongue pressed against the roof of his mouth, a bhikkhu beats down, constrains, and crushes mind with mind…
mn20:7.9: his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
mn20:8.1: “Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is giving attention to some sign, and owing to that sign there arise in him evil unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, with hate, and with delusion, then when he gives attention to some other sign connected with what is wholesome, any such evil unwholesome thoughts are abandoned in him and subside,
mn20:8.2: and with the abandoning of them his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
mn20:8.3: When he examines the danger in those thoughts…
mn20:8.5: When he tries to forget those thoughts and does not give attention to them…
mn20:8.7: When he gives attention to stilling the thought-formation of those thoughts…
mn20:8.9: When, with his teeth clenched and his tongue pressed against the roof of his mouth, he beats down, constrains, and crushes mind with mind, any such evil unwholesome thoughts are abandoned in him…
mn20:8.10: and his mind becomes steadied internally, quieted, brought to singleness, and concentrated.
mn20:8.11: This bhikkhu is then called a master of the courses of thought.
mn20:8.12: He will think whatever thought he wishes to think and he will not think any thought that he does not wish to think.
mn20:8.13: He has severed craving, flung off the fetters, and with the complete penetration of conceit he has made an end of suffering.”
mn20:8.14: That is what the Blessed One said.
mn20:8.15: The bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
